purpose: Assess ASVS V2 Validation and Business Logic against the authoritative deal command path, where the risk is not a missing control but an existing one being mistaken for compliance.
requiredInvariants: Each of the 13 V2 requirements carries its own decision and its own evidence.
The presence of a transaction, a lock or a validation pipe is not by itself a PASS; the control must be bound to a file and re-verified on every run.
A decision that names the deal lifecycle must state which of the two transition maps in the tree it rests on.
A requirement whose assessment cannot be honestly completed stays NOT_ASSESSED with the reason recorded, and still blocks finalPass.
FAIL is recorded and reported, never resolved by editing product logic.
Requirement prose from the standard must not be copied into the evidence artifact.
No product logic, dependency, production, REG.RU, DNS or database change.
acceptance: V2.3.1 names the authoritative command path and states that runtime-core carries a separate map it does not rest on.
The transaction and locking PASS decisions are bound to the lines where those mechanisms apply to a deal command.
The missing anti-automation control on the bulk-data endpoints is recorded as FAIL and is not softened by reference to an nginx configuration that no deployment file references.
V2.2.3 records applicability as decided and the assessment as deliberately withheld, with the reason stated.
An applicable-but-unassessed requirement is counted apart from an undecided one and still blocks finalPass.
The concurrent-scope guard accepts exactly the three authorized paths.
